sessions.title: Architecture design and doc governance
sessions.summary: Ran /init to create CLAUDE.md, then set up a GitHub Projects task-tracking workflow (correcting once after bulk-created issues without real discussion behind them were deleted). Did a deep architecture pass — component diagram, a local storage engine decision (SQLite chosen on a daily-write access-pattern analysis, put behind a WorkingStore interface after an earlier premature lock had to be walked back), dual legacy.json/legacy.db export formats, and a registry push-via-PR-with-pull-fallback design — then created manifest.md to define which doc owns which kind of information after duplicated reasoning across files made one correction cost four file edits.
sessions.next_steps: Review and commit/push the five modified/new docs (ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, IDEATION.md, research-log.md, manifest.md) sitting uncommitted locally; then resolve remaining open decisions (detector stack Node/TS vs Swift, legacy.json/legacy.db field-level schema, repo layout) before any actual code gets written.

sessions.title: Rust detector scaffold and SQLite schema design
sessions.summary: Resolved the detector-language decision (Rust, closing issue #1) and repo layout (single monorepo, closing issue #2), then hand-built a working first-pass scanner that walks /Applications and parses Info.plist for bundle ID/version, explaining Rust fundamentals along the way since this is the user's first Rust project. Designed a five-table SQLite schema (tools, scans, scan_results, usage_events, checkpoints) for the WorkingStore, after which the user chose to take over the ER/LLD diagramming themselves in excalidraw/system.excalidraw as a learning exercise. Also diagnosed a noisy atuin integration hook (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure on the Bash matcher in ~/.claude/settings.json) that fails because atuin isn't installed locally.
sessions.next_steps: User to finish the schema/ER design themselves in excalidraw/system.excalidraw; then translate it into Rust (rusqlite migration code) for the WorkingStore. Continue building remaining scanners (Homebrew Cellar, cargo, npm). Nothing from this session is committed yet — detector/ scaffold and doc updates (IDEATION.md, CLAUDE.md, research-log.md) since commit 34d853b are still local-only.

sessions.title: DBML schema design and catalog research
sessions.summary: Long hands-on LLD session where the user designed the WorkingStore schema themselves in dbdiagram.io (DBML), with me reviewing each draft: sources/tools/devices/users tables, JSON-attributes hybrid pattern, event-sourcing vs snapshot+diff, and a rigorous re-test of whether extensions belong under 'tools'. Backed decisions with live verification (sysinfo vs system_profiler on the real Mac, knowledgeC.db, brew info --json service field, crates.io adoption data, BrewUI precedent) and rewrote LESSONS.md as imperative guidelines.
sessions.next_steps: Settle the remaining schema forks (extensions carve-out, visibility_override/privacy mechanism, tool_events vs change_events), then start implementing the WorkingStore in Rust.

sessions.title: Diesel-backed WorkingStore and identity design
sessions.summary: Taught the Strategy/Adapter pattern and Rust fundamentals (vs. Java), then built a real Scanner/ScannerRegistry pipeline and switched the WorkingStore from raw rusqlite to Diesel (weighed ORM overhead vs. maintainability in depth first). Iterated the DBML schema through several rounds of real design pushback: rejected devices/users/user_devices as premature multi-device complexity, settled on single-user/single-machine scope for v1 with a minimal single-row local_identity table (platform_UUID, device_name, username, chip/memory/os attributes), and worked out how change-detection (device_tools vs. change_events/checkpoints) and future multi-device merging would need to work if ever built. Verified everything live against the real /Applications folder and the real local_identity resolution (system_profiler + whoami + sysinfo), and committed the working Applications-scanner + Diesel store in two commits.
sessions.next_steps: Add a second scanner (Homebrew Cellar/Cask) to prove the registry handles multiple sources for real. The change_events/checkpoints event-sourcing design and the privacy/visibility_override mechanism are still fully unbuilt. Commit the local_identity migration + identity.rs (done in-session but not yet committed to git).
